options.content:
# Trace RED and Service Graph

**What did the _caller_ actually experience?** Every latency figure on the Cassandra
dashboards is what Cassandra says about itself. These come from spans, so they cover
everything between the client and the answer: serialisation, network, coordinator
queueing and the replica read. When the two disagree, the difference is outside the
database.

**One producer writes these metric names.** The OTel collector spanmetrics and servicegraph
connectors, which carry no `source` label. Tempo's own metrics-generator is switched off: it wrote
the same metric names from the same spans and doubled every rate. Panels pin `source=""` so only
the collector is read.

**Units differ across families.** `traces_spanmetrics_duration_milliseconds` is in
**milliseconds**. `traces_service_graph_request_*_seconds` is in **seconds**. Cassandra's
`cassandra_client_request_latency_*` is in **microseconds**. Every panel names its unit.

Duration here is a real histogram, so `histogram_quantile` is correct on this page.

panels.title: Span rate
panels.description: Spans per second across every span name. Source: collector traces_spanmetrics_duration_milliseconds_count.

panels.title: Error ratio
panels.description: Share of spans with status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR. The numerator falls back to zero when no error series exists, so a clean run reads 0 rather than No data. The panel is still empty when no spans are flowing at all, because the denominator is then zero.

targets.expr: label_replace(100 * (sum by (cluster) (rate(traces_spanmetrics_calls_total{cluster=~"$cluster", source="", host_name=~"$host", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[$__rate_interval])) or 0 * sum by (cluster) (rate(traces_spanmetrics_calls_total{cluster=~"$cluster", source="", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]))) / sum by (cluster) (rate(traces_spanmetrics_calls_total{cluster=~"$cluster", source="", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

panels.title: p99 span duration (ms)
panels.description: 99th percentile across all span names. Unit: MILLISECONDS.

panels.title: Distinct span names
panels.description: How many span names the pipeline is currently reporting. A drop to zero means trace ingest has stopped, not that the database got quiet.

panels.title: Span Rate by $groupby (spans/s)
panels.description: The R in RED. Grouped by the $groupby variable. Honoured dimensions on this family: span_name, span_kind, status_code, service_name, host_name.

panels.title: Error Rate by status_code (spans/s)
panels.description: The E in RED, split by span status. STATUS_CODE_UNSET is the normal case; STATUS_CODE_ERROR is a failure the caller saw.

panels.title: Duration Percentiles by Span Name (ms)
panels.description: The D in RED. p50, p90 and p99 together so the shape of the distribution stays visible. Unit: MILLISECONDS. Real histogram, so histogram_quantile is valid.

targets.expr: label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (cluster, span_name, le) (rate(traces_spanmetrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]))), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.90, sum by (cluster, span_name, le) (rate(traces_spanmetrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]))), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (cluster, span_name, le) (rate(traces_spanmetrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]))), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

panels.title: p99 Duration by $groupby (ms)
panels.description: Same p99, grouped by the $groupby variable. Set $groupby to host_name to see whether one node is slower from the caller's point of view. Unit: MILLISECONDS.

panels.title: Mean Duration by $groupby (ms)
panels.description: sum/count, not a quantile. The mean moves when the bulk of the work changes; p99 moves when the tail changes. Unit: MILLISECONDS.

targets.expr: label_replace(sum by (cluster, $groupby) (rate(traces_spanmetrics_duration_milliseconds_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (cluster, $groupby) (rate(traces_spanmetrics_duration_milliseconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

panels.title: Span RED Table — rate, p99 and mean per span name
panels.description: One row per span name, sortable. Rate is spans/s, p99 and mean are in MILLISECONDS. Use it to find which statement dominates and which one is slow.

targets.expr: label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (cluster, span_name, le) (rate(traces_spanmetrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]))), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

label_replace(sum by (cluster, span_name) (rate(traces_spanmetrics_duration_milliseconds_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (cluster, span_name) (rate(traces_spanmetrics_duration_milliseconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

panels.title: Service graph — client side against server side (SECONDS)
Service Graph Request Rate by Edge (req/s)
panels.description: Collector service graph (source=""). One series per client to server edge. connection_type=database means the server side is a datastore, not another instrumented service.

targets.expr: label_replace(sum by (cluster, client, server, connection_type) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{cluster=~"$cluster", source=""}[$__rate_interval])), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

panels.title: Service Graph Failed Request Rate by Edge (req/s)
panels.description: The failed label exists only on the collector service graph (source=""); Tempo's generator does not emit it in this build.

targets.expr: label_replace(sum by (cluster, client, server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{cluster=~"$cluster", source="", failed="true"}[$__rate_interval])), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

panels.title: Edge Latency p99: Client Side vs Server Side (s)
panels.description: Two histograms for the same edge. The client histogram is measured at the caller; the server histogram is measured at the callee. Unit: SECONDS.

targets.expr: label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (cluster, client, server, le) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_client_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", source=""}[$__rate_interval]))), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (cluster, client, server, le) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_server_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", source=""}[$__rate_interval]))), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

panels.title: Client minus Server p99 — network plus queueing (s)
panels.description: The gap between what the caller timed and what the callee timed. That gap is network plus queueing, measured from the trace side. It is a different answer to the coordinator-versus-replica question than the MBeans give. Unit: SECONDS. CAVEAT: for connection_type=database edges the collector synthesises the server side from the same client span, so the delta is structurally zero until a genuine server span exists for the edge.

targets.expr: label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (cluster, client, server, le) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_client_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", source=""}[$__rate_interval]))) - histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (cluster, client, server, le) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_server_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", source=""}[$__rate_interval]))), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

panels.title: Edge Mean Latency: Client vs Server (s)
panels.description: sum/count for the same two histograms. The mean gap and the p99 gap answer different questions: a mean gap is steady overhead, a p99 gap is intermittent queueing. Unit: SECONDS.

targets.expr: label_replace(sum by (cluster, client, server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_client_seconds_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", source=""}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (cluster, client, server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_client_seconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster", source=""}[$__rate_interval])), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

label_replace(sum by (cluster, client, server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_server_seconds_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", source=""}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (cluster, client, server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_server_seconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster", source=""}[$__rate_interval])), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

panels.title: Client minus Server Mean — steady overhead (s)
panels.description: Mean version of the delta panel. Unit: SECONDS. Same caveat about synthesised server spans on database edges.

targets.expr: label_replace((sum by (cluster, client, server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_client_seconds_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", source=""}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (cluster, client, server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_client_seconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster", source=""}[$__rate_interval]))) - (sum by (cluster, client, server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_server_seconds_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", source=""}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (cluster, client, server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_server_seconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster", source=""}[$__rate_interval]))), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

panels.title: Service Graph Health (collector service_graph connector) — edges built, expired edges, dropped spans
panels.description: The OTel collector's service_graph connector on each node, per collector. Edges built is edges the connector completed and turned into service-graph metrics. Expired edges waited longer than the store's TTL for their matching span; dropped spans could not be added because the edge store was full (max_items). The collector exports the dropped-spans counter only after its first drop, so until then the query falls back to 0 for every host that builds edges. Either one non-zero means the graph is incomplete: read the delta panels above with suspicion. Tempo's metrics generator is off (processors: [] in tempo.yaml), so none of this comes from Tempo.

targets.expr: label_replace(sum by (cluster, host_name) (rate(otelcol_connector_servicegraph_dropped_spans_total{cluster=~"$cluster"}[$__rate_interval])) or 0 * sum by (cluster, host_name) (rate(otelcol_connector_servicegraph_edges_total{cluster=~"$cluster"}[$__rate_interval])), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

panels.title: Trace pipeline — is anything arriving at all?
Spans Received by Tempo (spans/s)
panels.description: Check this first. If it is zero, every panel above is stale by design and the problem is the sender, not the database.

panels.title: Spans Discarded, Refused and Truncated (per second)
panels.description: Loss inside Tempo, plus spans each node's OTel collector refused or failed before its span_metrics and service_graph connectors saw them. Anything non-zero here means the RED numbers above are computed from a sample, not from every request.

targets.expr: label_replace(sum by (cluster, host_name) (rate(otelcol_receiver_refused_spans_total{cluster=~"$cluster"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (cluster, host_name) (rate(otelcol_receiver_failed_spans_total{cluster=~"$cluster"}[$__rate_interval])), "cluster_name", "$1", "cluster", "(.+-[0-9a-f]{8})-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}")

panels.title: Connector Series (collector span_metrics and service_graph)
panels.description: Series the OTel collector's span_metrics and service_graph connectors produce, counted in Mimir per host. Each span name, status and dimension combination is a series, and each service-graph edge is a set of series. A count that keeps climbing means a label value is multiplying series. Tempo's metrics generator is off (processors: [] in tempo.yaml); these connectors are the only producer.

panels.title: Live Traces and Live-Store Queue
panels.description: Backlog on the storage side. Live traces are held in memory by Tempo's live store until they are cut into the WAL; the queue is WAL blocks waiting to be completed and flushed to the backend. A growing queue with a flat live-trace count means Tempo is accepting faster than it can write. Tempo 3 has no distributor queue (the distributor hands spans straight to the live store), so that series is gone.

list.description: The clusters this dashboard shows. Clusters of one tenant share one store, so every query filters by this variable.
list.label: Cluster
list.name: cluster

list.description: Derived from the collector spanmetrics family, so only nodes that emit spans appear. All expands to the explicit list; allValue is deliberately unset. Tempo-generator panels ignore this variable because that family has no host_name.
list.label: Host
list.name: host

list.description: Aggregation dimension for the RED panels. Only labels that exist on the collector spanmetrics family are offered; each panel names the dimension it honours.
list.label: Group by
list.name: groupby
